title: Kill Switch pattern: a revoked enforcement-point credential can be read as an outage
author: Santoshkumarpuppala
summary: The Kill Switch pattern merged in #26 could name one more residual risk: an interaction between Containment Actions step 2, Network and Tool Denial ([L67](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/53e0a28f9eb1ca4ce21f06b27b2453e696efd86a/workstreams/design-patterns/DRA...
inline_text:
The Kill Switch pattern merged in #26 could name one more residual risk: an interaction between Containment Actions step 2, Network and Tool Denial ([L67](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/53e0a28f9eb1ca4ce21f06b27b2453e696efd86a/workstreams/design-patterns/DRAFT-kill_switch_pattern.md?plain=1#L67)), and step 3, Credential Revocation ([L71](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/53e0a28f9eb1ca4ce21f06b27b2453e696efd86a/workstreams/design-patterns/DRAFT-kill_switch_pattern.md?plain=1#L71)). Where the enforcement point runs in the agent's workload, as an in-process SDK or a sidecar, and step 3 revokes the credential it presents to its policy service, the policy call that would carry step 2's denial comes back HTTP 401/403. An availability breaker or allow fallback that takes that response reopens tool dispatch at the moment of activation, through the revocation that Benefits says "permanently closes the lateral-movement surface" ([L127](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/53e0a28f9eb1ca4ce21f06b27b2453e696efd86a/workstreams/design-patterns/DRAFT-kill_switch_pattern.md?plain=1#L127)).

None of the three Residual Risks bullets ([L138-140](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/53e0a28f9eb1ca4ce21f06b27b2453e696efd86a/workstreams/design-patterns/DRAFT-kill_switch_pattern.md?plain=1#L138-L140)) covers this, and the file has no text on fallback, unavailability or 401/403. The pattern set already has the pieces: Circuit Breakers ([L75](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/53e0a28f9eb1ca4ce21f06b27b2453e696efd86a/workstreams/design-patterns/DRAFT-kill_switch_pattern.md?plain=1#L75)) counts error rates and halts when OPEN, and Approval Checkpoint reports an approval that cannot be checked as unavailable, separately from an integrity failure (V8, [L72](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/53e0a28f9eb1ca4ce21f06b27b2453e696efd86a/workstreams/design-patterns/DRAFT-approval_checkpoint_pattern.md?plain=1#L72)).

Proposed bullet after Byzantine Control Exploitation:

> **Revocation Read as an Outage:** An enforcement point that runs in the agent's workload and authenticates to its policy service with a credential that Credential Revocation invalidates gets HTTP 401/403 from that service, and an availability breaker or allow fallback that takes that response reopens the tool dispatch that Network and Tool Denial closed. The enforcement point treats the rejection as a refusal and blocks the call. The rejection counts toward the Circuit Breakers counters and stays out of any availability breaker or fallback.

Scope: an HTTP 401/403 answer to the enforcement point's own credential; an unreachable policy service is outside it. Read from the text at `53e0a28f`, not run. Happy to open the PR, or to put it in Runtime Policy Enforcement (3.1) once that has a draft.
